page: Amazon Web Services t3a.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose instance utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at 2.2 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reflect the burstable nature of the CPU allocation. Sustained compute tests, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU benchmarks, fall into the bottom 10% category. Similarly, memory bandwidth and compression tasks show weak to poor performance under continuous load. However, the processor supports hardware-accelerated cryptography, allowing the Passmark CPU encryption test to achieve an average rating in the middle 50% tier.

This instance type offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that experience intermittent spikes in demand rather than continuous high CPU utilization. Because it relies on a CPU credit system, sustained heavy processing will deplete credits and throttle performance. It is best suited for general-purpose workloads with variable resource requirements, such as development environments, code repositories, low-traffic web servers, and microservices.
